articles.title: Comparative Efficacy of Leukocyte-Rich and Leukocyte-Poor PRP for Lateral Epicondylitis on Isokinetic and Isometric Upper Limb Strength under an Identical Rehabilitation Protocol: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.authors: Walecka J, Kaszynski J, Cisowski P, Kaczmarek P, Lubiatowski P
articles.outcomes: Peak isometric wrist extensor torque at 12 months (primary); isokinetic elbow flexor and extensor torque, isometric wrist flexor torque, and hand grip strength (secondary)
articles.take_home: Both types of platelet-rich plasma improved wrist strength over 12 months, but the improvement was no better than saline injections. PRP may help as part of a rehabilitation programme, but it does not appear to be essential for long-term strength recovery in tennis elbow.

articles.title: Understanding Clinical Practice Variation in Dental Prophylaxis After Total Shoulder Arthroplasty in ASES Surgeons: A Call for Shoulder-Specific Guidelines.
articles.authors: Basdavanos AA, Montgomery EP, Muffly MT, Navarro RA
articles.population: American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons (ASES) members
articles.outcomes: Antibiotic prophylaxis practices for dental procedures after total shoulder arthroplasty; surgeon experience with dental-related infections; support for shoulder-specific guidelines
articles.take_home: Most shoulder surgeons (89.3%) recommend antibiotics for dental procedures after shoulder replacement, though hip and knee guidelines do not routinely recommend this. Surgeons who had experienced or were unsure about a shoulder infection linked to dental work were much more likely to prescribe antibiotics, suggesting that practice varies based on individual experience rather than evidence.

articles.title: Failure Patterns Leading to Revision After Distal Humerus Fracture Fixation: A Multicenter Study.
articles.authors: Elze M, Ellwein A, Bulow HJ, Hollinger B, Burkhart K, Schmalzl J, et al.
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing revision surgery after distal humerus fracture fixation
articles.sample_size: 491 patients across 11 specialized centres (411 included in primary analysis)
articles.outcomes: Revision surgery causes categorized as mechanical (43.1%), functional (41.4%), or infectious (15.6%) complications; time to revision; risk factors for each complication type
articles.take_home: Distal humerus fractures that fail after initial surgery do so through different mechanisms rather than one common pathway. Open fractures are at much higher risk of infection, whilst implant slipping is the most common mechanical problem, and younger patients are slightly more likely to need revision for functional problems.

articles.title: Association Between Glenohumeral Bony Morphology and Anterior Shoulder Instability: An Advanced Three-Dimensional Analysis.
articles.authors: Jin H, Pang L, Chen S, Zhang G, Li J, Huang Y, et al.
articles.study_type: Cross-sectional observational study using three-dimensional CT imaging
articles.population: Adults with recurrent anterior shoulder instability and matched controls
articles.sample_size: 210 participants (105 with anterior shoulder instability, 105 controls)
articles.outcomes: Glenohumeral bone measurements including glenoid index, glenoid version angle, glenoid inclination angle, glenoid depth, humeral head containment angle, and humeral head-to-glenoid diameter ratio
articles.take_home: People with recurrent anterior shoulder instability have characteristic bone shape differences, particularly a wider glenoid socket and shallower socket depth, and these features were also present in their unaffected shoulder, suggesting these anatomical differences may predispose to instability.

articles.title: National Trends in Utilization, Reimbursement, and Patient Demographics for Arthroscopic Subacromial Decompression, Biceps Tenodesis, and Distal Clavicle Excision in the Medicare Population.
articles.authors: Dinesh A, Burkhart RJ, Salata MJ, Calcei JG, Voos JE, Apostolakos JM, et al.
articles.study_type: Descriptive epidemiology study analysing national trends using Medicare claims data
articles.population: Medicare beneficiaries in the United States
articles.sample_size: 498,400 subacromial decompressions, 73,668 arthroscopic biceps tenodesis, 214,015 distal clavicle excisions, and 82,398 open biceps tenodesis procedures billed between 2013 and 2023
articles.outcomes: Trends in procedure utilisation rates, inflation-adjusted reimbursement, patient demographics, regional and rural-urban variations
articles.take_home: Between 2013 and 2023, subacromial decompression and distal clavicle excision procedures declined significantly in Medicare patients, whilst biceps tenodesis more than doubled, reflecting changes in clinical practice. Reimbursement fell for all three procedures, and notable geographic and rural-urban disparities in access and payment persist.

articles.title: Predictors of PROMIS Pain Interference Two Years After Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair.
articles.authors: Blommer JM, Funk K, Kinney SL, Healey K, Patankar A, McCurdy MA, et al.
articles.study_type: Prospective cohort study from orthopaedic registry
articles.population: Adults undergoing arthroscopic rotator cuff repair
articles.sample_size: 152 patients (75% of 203 enrolled) completed two-year follow-up
articles.outcomes: PROMIS Pain Interference score at two years post-surgery; predictors included preoperative shoulder function (ASES), depression scores, and comorbidity index
articles.take_home: Patients with better shoulder function before surgery had less pain interference two years after rotator cuff repair. Patients with more medical conditions or depression before surgery were more likely to experience worse pain interference after surgery.

articles.title: A Safe Medial Column Screw Strategy for Transcondylar Humerus Fractures in the Elderly: CT-Based Analysis of Screw Diameter and Insertion Trajectory.
articles.authors: Totoki Y, Yanagisawa Y, Ikumi A, Watanabe Y, Eda Y, Yoneda N, et al.
articles.population: Elderly patients (aged 65 years and over) and younger adults
articles.outcomes: Maximum safe screw diameter and insertion angles for medial column screws in distal humerus fractures
articles.take_home: Most elderly patients have enough space in their upper arm bone to accommodate a 5 mm screw in the medial column, though the exact size needs to be tailored to individual anatomy. Men generally have larger spaces than women.

articles.title: Minimum 10-year survivorship and risk factors for failure following reverse total shoulder arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Saad Berreta R, Badin D, Fox H, Koyejo LD, Almasri S, Ashkar A, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent reverse total shoulder arthroplasty between 2010 and 2013 with healthcare claims at least 10 years after surgery
articles.outcomes: 10-year survival rate was 95.0%. Revision surgery occurred in 5.2% of patients, with mean time to revision of 2.5 years. Risk factors for failure: younger age, male sex, prior rotator cuff repair, and primary diagnosis of glenohumeral osteoarthritis.
articles.take_home: Reverse shoulder replacement has excellent long-term results, with 95 out of 100 patients not needing further surgery at 10 years. Younger patients, men, and those with previous rotator cuff surgery or arthritis were more likely to need revision surgery.

articles.title: Temporal Macrophage Activation Is Reduced by CCR2 Knockout in a Murine Subacromial Impingement Model.
articles.authors: Covello MR, Carballo CB, Pedaprolu K, Yao VJH, Ranga S, Piacentini A, et al.
articles.study_type: Laboratory study using a mouse model of rotator cuff impingement
articles.population: Mice (C57BL/6J wild type and CCR2 knockout strains)
articles.sample_size: 64 mice total (40 wild type with impingement, 20 CCR2 knockout with impingement, 4 sham controls)
articles.outcomes: Macrophage activation measured by PET imaging; gene expression patterns; histological changes in tendons; biomechanical properties of tendons
articles.take_home: In this mouse study, rotator cuff damage caused early inflammation with immune cell activation peaking at 3 to 7 days. Mice lacking the CCR2 protein showed reduced inflammation and less tendon damage, suggesting that CCR2 might be a useful target for new treatments to reduce inflammation in rotator cuff disease.

articles.title: Static versus dynamic superior augmentation in anterior latissimus dorsi and teres major tendon transfer for anterosuperior irreparable rotator cuff tears with narrow acromiohumeral distances.
articles.authors: Baek CH, Lim C, Kim JG, Kim BT, Kim SJ
articles.population: Patients with anterosuperior irreparable rotator cuff tears and narrow acromiohumeral distance
articles.sample_size: 34 patients (14 in static augmentation group, 20 in dynamic augmentation group)
articles.outcomes: Pain, patient-reported outcome measures, active range of motion, muscle strength, acromiohumeral distance, Hamada grade, and structural integrity of repair
articles.take_home: Dynamic augmentation using middle trapezius tendon transfer combined with latissimus and teres major transfer produced better improvements in overhead movement and strength, and had much lower failure rates, compared with static augmentation using superior capsular reconstruction in patients with severe rotator cuff tears and limited space under the shoulder blade.

articles.title: The learning curve associated with robotic-assisted shoulder arthroplasty: A feasibility study.
articles.authors: Boekel P, Grant A, Doma K, Morse L
articles.population: Patients undergoing MAKO robotic-assisted reverse shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Operative time, cognitive workload measured by NASA Task Load Index (NASA-TLX) score, intraoperative complications
articles.take_home: The surgeon's cognitive workload improved after 3 to 5 robotic-assisted shoulder operations, showing they became more comfortable with the new technology. Cognitive workload was a better measure of learning than how long operations took.

articles.title: Infection risk following total shoulder arthroplasty in patients with diabetic foot ulcers.
articles.authors: Catanzaro C, Guareschi M, Ninness H, Rogalski B, Eichinger JK, Friedman RJ
articles.population: Diabetic patients undergoing primary total shoulder arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 56,482 diabetic patients (2,404 with diabetic foot ulcers)
articles.outcomes: Postoperative sepsis, deep wound infection, and periprosthetic joint infection at 90 days and 1 year
articles.take_home: Diabetic patients with foot ulcers who have shoulder replacement surgery have significantly higher risks of infection and sepsis compared to diabetic patients without foot ulcers. This information should be discussed with patients before surgery and may require closer monitoring afterwards.

articles.title: Magnetic resonance imaging-based cortical thickness as a predictor of osteoporosis in rotator cuff tears .
articles.authors: Keatisuwan S, Rattanavarinchai J, Sisayanarane T, Lumdee K, Saowatanpong N, Iamwat J, et al.
articles.population: Female patients with rotator cuff tears undergoing shoulder MRI
articles.outcomes: Proximal humeral cortical bone thickness measurements on MRI compared with osteoporosis diagnosis on DXA scanning; cortical bone thickness average (CBTavg) below 4.5 mm showed 100% sensitivity and 86% specificity for detecting osteoporosis
articles.take_home: Bone thickness measurements already visible on routine shoulder MRI scans could be used to spot osteoporosis in patients having rotator cuff repair, avoiding the need for extra scans and radiation. The authors suggest referring patients with very thin bone on MRI for bone density testing, but stress these findings need to be tested in other patient groups before being used in routine practice.
